images.title: Median zero, big total
images.purpose: Show that when most sorted scores are 0 the median is 0, while a few big scores still make the mean large.
images.composition: One sorted row of 7 score cards across the centre, the middle card highlighted, with two short result lines below; generous white space.
exact_structure: A single row of 7 equal rounded cards in sorted order, left to right: 0, 0, 0, 0, 12, 90, 108.
All 7 cards have a teal (#0072B2) outline and dark numbers; the 1st to 3rd cards (0, 0, 0) and the 5th to 7th cards (12, 90, 108) are white inside.
The 4th card (the middle one, a 0, with 3 cards on each side) is filled light reddish purple (#CC79A7) with a reddish purple arrow pointing down at it from above.
Below the row, line one reads Median = 0 under the highlighted card.
Below that, line two reads Mean = 210 ÷ 7 = 30, in green (#009E73).
rejection: a number of 0 cards other than 4
a highlighted card other than the 4th
the 0 cards greyed or struck out, as if a zero were not a value
images.takeaway: The median looks only at the middle score, but the mean uses every run, so a few big scores lift it.
images.description: Seven sorted score cards 0, 0, 0, 0, 12, 90, 108 with the middle 0 highlighted as the median and the mean shown as 210 ÷ 7 = 30.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Ask how many cards are on each side of the highlighted one, then compare with the eleven England batters.

image_decisions.why: The sorted row makes it visible how the middle value can be 0 while the total is large.
